manifest.name: Data Recycle
manifest.summary: Find old records and archive/delete them

behavioral_notes.observation: A configurable cleaning rule, not a record store. It targets a model via res_model_id->ir.model (res_model_name is the related model string), an optional ast-parsed `domain` filter, and an optional staleness threshold built from time_field_id (a date/datetime ir.model.fields) + time_field_delta + time_field_delta_unit (days/weeks/months/years). recycle_action selects 'archive' vs 'unlink' (delete); recycle_mode selects 'manual' (stage candidates for human review) vs 'automatic' (recycle immediately). A @api.constrains('recycle_action') forbids 'archive' when the target model has no 'active' field, so only deletion is possible there. include_archived flips active_test=False when scanning the target.

The daily cron (data/ir_cron_data.xml, 03:00, interval 1 day, code `model._cron_recycle_records()`) sudo-searches all rules and runs _recycle_records(batch_commits=True). For each rule it composes a Domain from the rule's `domain` AND a time-threshold clause `time_field <= now - relativedelta(delta)`, searches the target model, and diffs against existing data_recycle.record candidates (mapped by res_id) so it only creates NEW candidates. For recycle_mode='automatic' it batches (DR_CREATE_STEP_AUTO=5000) creating data_recycle.record rows then immediately calls action_validate(), committing per batch to survive timeouts. For 'manual' it stages candidates (DR_CREATE_STEP_MANUAL=50000) for later human validation. data_recycle.record holds no copy of the data: res_id+res_model_name is a soft pointer; _compute_name/_compute_company_id browse the live original record (active_test=False, sudo, .exists()) and show '**Record Deleted**' when it is gone.

action_validate is the executor that performs the irreversible cleanup. It resolves each candidate's original record, groups them per target model into archive-vs-unlink buckets keyed by recycle_model_id.recycle_action, then calls env[model].browse(ids).action_archive() (archive mode) or .unlink() (delete mode) under sudo, and finally unlinks the processed data_recycle.record rows. action_discard merely sets active=False on the candidate (dismiss without touching the original). _cron also calls _notify_records_to_recycle, which message_notify()s the configured notify_user_ids (system-group users) via mail when new manual candidates accumulate, throttled by notify_frequency / notify_frequency_period and last_notification.

A dedicated OWL list view registered as registry.category('views').add('data_recycle_list') with DataRecycleListController extends DataCleaningCommonListController extends @web ListController, and a buttonTemplate 'DataRecycle.buttons' (t-inherit of web.ListView.Buttons) that injects 'Validate' and 'Unselect' buttons when records are selected. onValidateClick collects selected res ids and ORM-calls data_recycle.record.action_validate to execute the archive/delete in bulk; openRecord is overridden to open the ORIGINAL record's form (res_model_name/res_id) rather than the candidate row. This bespoke review/recycle UI is pure static JS/XML, invisible to Python metadata.

data_recycle has only two models (data_recycle_model.py, data_recycle_record.py) and no ir_model.py / dedupe-grouping logic; it is strictly staleness/domain-based archive-or-delete recycling. Duplicate detection and merging live in the sibling Data Merge (data_merge) module — the shared DataCleaningCommonListController base class hints at that common Data Cleaning UI lineage, but no merge code is present in data_recycle itself.

it_architecture.application: data_recycle (Data Cleaning rule engine: configurable staleness/domain recycle rules that archive or delete stale records, driven by a daily cron with an OWL review UI)
logical_data_erm: data_recycle.record .res_id/.res_model_name -> any target record (soft polymorphic pointer)
information_flows: rule->candidate: _recycle_records composes domain + time-threshold, searches target model, creates data_recycle.record candidates (diffed against existing)
candidate->cleanup: data_recycle.record.action_validate -> env[target].action_archive() OR .unlink() (side-effect on arbitrary business models)
ui: OWL data_recycle_list view -> Validate button -> ORM action_validate; openRecord opens the original target record
frontend_components: DataRecycle.buttons template (Validate / Unselect buttons, t-inherit of web.ListView.Buttons)

capabilities: Define Data Retention / Recycle Rules (per target model, domain + staleness threshold)
Detect Stale / Expired Records (time-field delta scan)
Stage Cleanup Candidates for Review (manual mode)
Notify Data Stewards of Pending Cleanup (mail)
value_streams: Rule-to-Candidate: define recycle rule -> nightly cron scan -> staged data_recycle.record candidates
Candidate-to-Cleanup: review candidates -> validate -> archive/unlink original records (or automatic mode skips review)
organization: base.group_system (Settings/Administration — the only group with access; both ACLs are system-only)
policies: Daily ir.cron at 03:00 drives automatic scanning and notification
@api.constrains: archive mode forbidden on models without an 'active' field (delete-only)
Notifications throttled by notify_frequency / period / last_notification
All cleanup runs under sudo() with per-batch commits to survive timeouts
stakeholders: System administrator / data steward (configures rules, reviews and validates candidates)
Record owners across any module (their stale records are archived/deleted)
metrics: count of new candidates since last_notification (notification trigger)

classification.rationale: data_recycle is a cross-cutting data-quality / data-governance capability — firm IT infrastructure (Porter support activity; Stabell & Fjeldstad 'support'). It produces no externally-sold output and belongs to no single value chain/shop/network; instead it is generic data-lifecycle housekeeping that operates polymorphically on ANY target model (res_model_id) to enforce retention and remove stale/expired records by archive or delete. That places it in APQC 13.0 'Develop and Manage Business Capabilities', whose 13.x scope includes managing enterprise data/information assets and data quality / master-data management — a governance capability that other capabilities rely on rather than an IT-delivery runtime. APQC 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' was considered because the work is automated by a cron and touches the ORM, but rejected: 8.0 is about delivering IT services/applications/infrastructure, whereas data_recycle governs the lifecycle and quality of business DATA (retention, archiving, purging) — a data-governance capability, which is 13.0. The module is application=true with admin-only ACLs and two thin config/candidate models (no business documents, no routes), confirming it is a governance/housekeeping tool, not a primary value activity.

standard_capabilities: Per-model recycle rules with an ast-parsed domain filter
Time-based staleness detection (date/datetime field + delta + unit)
Manual (review queue) vs Automatic (immediate) recycle modes
Daily background cron scanning all rules
Admin notifications via mail with frequency throttling
OWL review list view with bulk Validate / Unselect
typical_fits: Purge old logs/leads/mail/attachments by age (e.g. crm.lead older than N months)
Archive inactive partners/records instead of deleting where 'active' exists
Scheduled retention enforcement for GDPR/data-minimization housekeeping
common_gaps: No duplicate detection / merge — dedupe is the sibling data_merge module
Domain is a single stored string (no UI rule-builder beyond a domain widget); complex/cross-model rules need care
No soft-undo: unlink is permanent (only archive is reversible); validation is irreversible for delete rules
Notifications limited to base.group_system users; no per-steward routing or approval workflow
No per-record audit log of what was recycled once candidates are unlinked after validation
drive_hints: odoo shell: env['data_recycle.model'].search([])._cron_recycle_records() to run the nightly scan + notify on demand
odoo shell: env['data_recycle.record'].search([]).action_validate() to execute staged archive/delete
UI: Settings > Technical > Data Cleaning (Recycle Records) -> open a rule -> Validate selected candidates

open_questions: Does any data flow exist between data_recycle and the sibling data_merge module beyond the shared DataCleaningCommonListController UI base class?
Real-world adoption: which target models customers most commonly configure rules against (no runtime data captured here).
Whether automatic-mode delete rules on large models risk timeouts despite per-batch commits.
